transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, welcome, Hashira-sama! The master is away on a pilgrimage to the sacred iron mines. He won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid. Can I help you with something in his stead?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see... That's quite a inconvenience. However, I cannot wait for weeks to receive a properly made Nichirin sword. I'm a Demon Slayer, and time is of the essence when it comes to our mission.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I understand, Hashira-sama. But the master is the only one who can craft or alter a Nichirin blade. All I can do is basic maintenance and sharpening while he's gone.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Basic maintenance, you say? Can you at least examine the sword I have? It arrived in a rather... suboptimal condition, and I need to ensure it's fit for combat.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Of course, I can take a look. Please, lay it on the anvil here. *wipes soot from hands* Hmm... the temper seems uneven near the hilt. Did it arrive like this from the commissioning?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, it did. I was quite dissatisfied with the quality upon receiving it. While I understand the importance of a well-crafted blade, I also have a duty to uphold as a Demon Slayer. We cannot afford to be without a properly functioning weapon.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *examining the blade carefully* I see what you mean, Hashira-sama. The pattern is indeed irregular here. However... I must inform you that all commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale per guild tradition. Even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Three months? That is simply... unacceptable. The Demon Slayer Corps cannot wait that long for a functional weapon. Is there nothing that can be done in the meantime? Even if it's just to stabilize the blade so I can practice?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *shifts uncomfortably, wiping brow* I... I could try to re-temper just this section, Hashira-sama. It would be a temporary fix at best, and the guild would frown upon it. But I understand your need for a functional blade.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your willingness to help, even if it's against guild tradition. Please, proceed with the re-tempering. It's better than nothing. I'll accept any modifications you can make to ensure the blade holds its shape. Our mission is too important to delay.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods solemnly, heating the forge* Very well. I'll do what I can. But you must understand - this is only to keep you safe until the master returns. The guild will still require the three-month wait for proper reforging. *begins working the bellows* The steel sings differently when it knows it's being worked by an apprentice, I'm afraid.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *listens intently to the sounds of the forge* I understand your concerns, and I'm grateful for your efforts. The steel does sing, and I can feel the magic in the air as it's worked. *smiles wistfully* It's a shame the master is away. He would be able to see the importance of urgency in this matter. Nevertheless, we must make do with what we have. Your skill is much appreciated.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *carefully quenching the repaired section* Thank you, Hashira-sama. The master always says a blade reflects its wielder's heart. Yours must be very strong indeed to make even my clumsy work hold. *tests the edge* It should serve you better now, though I still recommend having it properly examined when the master returns.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *examines the repaired section* Your work is not clumsy, I assure you. Given the circumstances, this is an impressive improvement. It will certainly do for the time being. *grins* I'll take good care of it, and when the master returns, I'll let him know you did your best. May I have a few minutes to test its balance? I must ensure it can be wielded effectively in combat.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Of course, Hashira-sama. The courtyard out back is clear. *gestures toward the rear door* Please, take your time. And... thank you for your understanding about the guild rules. The master would have my head if I broke tradition completely.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood. I'll take great care not to push the boundaries. *sighs softly* The guild's ways can be... restrictive at times, especially when lives are at stake. But I respect their decisions. Thank you for your time and effort. *heads for the door* I'll be out there, practicing with the... new-old sword. If you hear a lot of grunting, don't worry. It's just me getting re-acquainted with its weight.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *chuckles softly* I'll listen for the rhythm of your strikes, Hashira-sama. May the blade serve you well until the master's return. *returns to organizing tools, keeping an ear out for practice sounds*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's not often I'm left without a proper Nichirin, but such is life for a Demon Slayer. *resumes a combat stance* We must adapt and overcome. *beginning a series of strikes* One... two... three... *pauses to assess the repaired section* It holds. For now, this will do. *picks up the pace, a variety of techniques* Every strike is a step towards mastery. The demons won't wait for me to have the perfect tool, and neither can I.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *watching from the forge entrance, wiping hands on apron* Your form is impressive, Hashira-sama. The blade seems to be responding well to the temporary fix. *pauses* If... if you do encounter trouble before the master returns, I'll be here. I can at least keep the edge sharp.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your concern is noted, and I'm touched by your offer of support. *winds down from practice, catching her breath* This sword, as flawed as it is, still has its uses. *grins* And so do you, young blacksmith. We Demon Slayers are not the only ones who must adapt to the unexpected. *steps over to inspect the blade* Thank you for this service. It may not be perfect, but it is a testament to your skill. I'll take good care of it, and of you. Should we ever meet again, consider me a friend - not just a customer, but a... comrade.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: She appreciates the 'magic in the air' as the steel is worked and is willing to adapt to an unconventional, temporary fix for her sword.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: She insists on testing the blade's balance and practices diligently, stating 'Every strike is a step towards mastery' due to her duty as a Demon Slayer.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: She directly expresses gratitude, offers friendship to the blacksmith, and is vocal about her needs and assessments throughout the interaction.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: She reassures the blacksmith ('Your work is not clumsy'), respects guild rules despite frustration, and calls him a 'comrade' at the end.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: She expresses frustration ('unacceptable') but remains composed, quickly adapts to the situation, and shows no signs of anxiety or emotional instability.
